name: Bazluth
overview: Bazluth was a male member of the tribe of Levi who served as a temple servant. His role as a temple servant places him within the Levitical duties related to the worship and maintenance of the temple, reflecting the tribe's God-ordained responsibilities. There are no additional notes recorded about his life or character.
namesAndTitles: The individual is known by the names Bazluth and Bazlith, as recorded in Ezra 2:52 and Nehemiah 7:54 respectively. Neither name has a provided meaning or divine origin, indicating they are proper names without explicit theological significance noted in Scripture.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture identifies Bazluth as a descendant of Levi, situating him within the Levitical lineage. Beyond this tribal association, no further family relationships are documented in the biblical record.
scriptureSignificance: Bazluth's significance lies in his role as a temple servant among the Levites, highlighting his participation in the restoration and function of the temple community after the exile. His mention in Ezra and Nehemiah underscores the careful record-keeping of those who returned to Jerusalem to reestablish worship according to God's covenant. As a Levite, Bazluth exemplifies faithfulness to God's appointed order in the post-exilic period.
